item.title: The Saudi and Gulf State Militaries Are Looking Very Hollow
item.description: The Gulf is in turmoil. Saudi Arabia, which for decades has dominated the region, using its oil wealth to command the attention and often obeisance of half the world, is tottering on its foundations. Civilians are being killed, US personnel evacuated. Its principal airports are intermittently closed by Houthi missiles. The rich are taking flight as best they can, and overseas pilgrims are wary about visiting.
item.dc:creator: Max Hastings

item.title: Political Corruption: New Laws Are the Only Way to Stop It
item.description: If you think President Donald Trump’s administration has a corruption problem, you are not alone: Even many Republicans are worried. But if you think the way to address it is simply to prosecute the offenders, you are sadly mistaken: As recent events illustrate, it will take new laws to bring the wrongdoers to justice.
item.dc:creator: Barbara McQuade

item.title: Election Deniers on the Ballot in 2026 Don't Deserve to Win
item.description: President Donald Trump did not win the 2020 presidential election, but there are 193 candidates in 41 states on the November ballot who won’t reject his “Big Lie” that he did. Half of all Republicans still believe his falsehoods, and few candidates are willing to publicly counter them.
item.dc:creator: Mary Ellen Klas

item.title: Elon Musk’s Plan to Give SpaceX Stock to Kids Is Another Empty Promise
item.description: The SpaceX CEO’s pledge to hand out shares to kids doesn’t exactly ring of sincerity.
item.dc:creator: Brooke Sample
